'''Georges Darmois''' (24 June 1888 – 3 January 1960) was a French [[mathematician]] and statistician.  He pioneered in the theory of [[Sufficiency (statistics)|sufficiency]], in [[stellar statistics]], and in [[factor analysis]]. He was also one of the first French mathematicians to teach British mathematical statistics.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Bor | first1=Bernard |editor1-link=Chris Heyde |editor-last1=Heyde |editor-first1=C. C. |editor2-link=Eugene Seneta |editor-last2=Seneta |editor-first2=E. |editor-last3=Crepel |editor-first3=P. |editor-last4=Fienberg |editor-first4=S.E. |editor-last5=Gani |editor-first5=J. |year=2001 |chapter=George Darmois |title=Statisticians of the Centuries |location=New York |publisher=Springer |pages=382–385 |isbn=0-387-95329-9 }}</ref>

He is one of the eponyms of the [[Koopman&ndash;Pitman&ndash;Darmois theorem]] and sufficient statistics and [[exponential family|exponential families]].

== Biography ==
Darmois was born on 24 June 1888 in [[Éply]]. He was admitted to [[École normale supérieure]] in 1906 and passed subsequently the [[agrégation]] de mathematiques in 1909. From 1911 to 1914, he was a qualified assistant (agrégé préparateur) at the [[École normale supérieure]], where his scientific activities were directed by Émile Borel who rapidly appreciated his talent.

Darmois earned his [[doctorate]] from the [[University of Paris]] in 1921. He defended a thesis on algebraic curves and partial differential equations before the jury consisting of [[Émile Picard]] and [[Édouard Goursat]]. In 1949, he succeeded [[Maurice René Fréchet]] as the Chair of Calculus of Probabilities and Mathematical Physics at the University of Paris, who had himself succeeded [[Émile Borel]].<ref>{{Citation |last=Roy |first=R. |year=1960 |title=Georges Darmois, 1888&ndash;1960 |journal=[[Journal of the Royal Statistical Society]] |series=Series A (General) |volume=123 |issue=4 |pages=520–522 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.2397-2327.1960.tb00736.x | doi = <!-- none: journal sold and Wiley will thus NOT register this DOI --> |jstor=2343305 }}</ref> His research spanned several fields of pure and applied mathematics, including [[geometry]], [[general relativity]], [[physics]], [[statistics]], [[time series]], and [[econometrics]].<ref>{{Citation |last=Roy |first=René|year=1961 |title=Georges Darmois, 1888&ndash;1960 |journal=[[Econometrica]]|volume=29|issue=1|pages=80–83|doi=10.2307/1907690|jstor=1907690}}</ref>

He was elected fellow of the [[Econometric Society]] in 1952.<ref>{{Cite web |date= |url=https://www.econometricsociety.org/society/organization-and-governance/fellows/memoriam |title=In Memory of Fellows of the Econometric Society |publisher= Econometric Society |access-date=24 July 2016}}</ref>
In 1955 he was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].<ref>[http://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm View/Search Fellows of the ASA] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616161612/https://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm |date=2016-06-16 }}, accessed 2016-07-23.</ref> He was also the president of [[International Statistical Institute]] from 1953 until 1960.

==Contributions==
His scientific contributions include:
* Giving the first rigorous proof of [[Cramér–Rao bound|Fréchet–Darmois–Cramér–Rao inequality]], also known as Cramér–Rao bound, in 1945 independently from Rao and Cramér.
* Developing the notion of [[Exponential family|Koopman–Darmois family]] of distributions also known as the exponential family of distributions.
* Establishing [[Koopman&ndash;Pitman&ndash;Darmois theorem]]
* Characterizing Gaussian distributions with [[Darmois–Skitovich theorem]]
